Symmetrizing the primal quadratic form cannot increase any Banach--Mazur distortion, so the single free scalar truly captures all linear isomorphisms. All polar vertex types are classified by parity and the optional branch crossing is ordered after the primal crossing. Explicit derivative tests prove the unique minimum and opposite parity behavior. 56 exact rational checks of the primal and polar spectra corroborate the proof; no finite enumeration is used as a universal argument.
